scope: Automatic atomic caching of the native same-origin Realm HTML response preserves response policy headers. The host is already loaded and Service Worker controlled; both host and application resource servers close their sockets, independent network requests fail, and a new Runtime creates a fresh iframe, mounts the cached module graph, and handles a real click.
relatedFixes: offline-cache automatically includes the required native Realm document

tests: atomically activates a host-owned application cache and serves it offline
creates a new native Realm and mounts the complete cached module graph while offline

iterations.cause: The test omitted an emitted static bootstrap helper. WebKit also failed native cached iframe navigation under setOffline(true).
Only the native WebKit setOffline iframe navigation limitation remained.

nativeControl.result: Without framework code, Chromium and Firefox pass setOffline and socket-failure cases. WebKit reports an internal navigation error with setOffline(true), but passes when the real server closes connections.

limits: The failed test graph and browser offline simulation are not framework red/green evidence.
Actual Safari offline behavior and initial page loading after a complete browser shutdown were not tested.
Bootstrap and application dependency graphs remain explicit; query parameters are not ignored.
Legacy cache records must be cached again to include the native Realm HTML resource.
